verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:142-158, Step 1.5 item 5: "5. **Cross-reference the phase's spec requirement bank, if one exists.** ... Look for the relevant spec at `docs/milestones/<M>/specs/<NNN>-<slug>/spec.md` (the `specify` skill's canonical output path; glob `docs/milestones/*/specs/*/spec.md` and match by feature slug or branch name if more than one candidate exists). If found, read its `US-xxx` user stories and check each one against both the diff and the coverage map:" and lines 151-153: "- **Promised but never touched** — a distinct, new category: a `US-xxx` story that appears in *neither* the diff nor the existing docs."
verdicts.reasoning: Verified on disk. The quoted skill sentence exists (spans lines 151-152, claim said 152 — close enough, the quote is accurate). KICKOFF 1234-1236 asks for exactly the skill's own numbered sub-step: the coverage map built against the spec's US-xxx story bank *as well as* the diff, so an untouched requirement is flagged. The skill does all of it — reads US-xxx stories, checks each against both diff and coverage map, defines 'Promised but never touched' as a distinct category, and surfaces it in the PR body (line 327: 'promised-but-never-touched stories (`US-xxx` items absent from both the diff and the docs; flag as a possible scope gap, not just a doc gap)'). I checked the one thing that could have made this load-bearing: whether `SPEC/spec.md` supplies a non-default path. It does not — KICKOFF line 16 defines `SPEC/` = `docs/milestones/<M>/specs/<NNN>-<slug>/`, byte-identical to the skill's line 145 default. The only other candidate was that the skill's item 5 is conditional ('if one exists', line 142; 'If no spec.md exists for this phase, skip this cross-reference silently', line 157) while KICKOFF asserts existence — but that assertion changes no behavior, since the skill uses the spec whenever it is there. Nothing survives as an operator parameter.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:168 "Read each documentation file and cross-reference it against the diff." and SKILL.md:137-140 "4. **Architecture diagram drift detection.** If `docs/global/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md` (or any doc) contains ASCII diagrams or Mermaid blocks, extract entity names (modules, services, data flows) from the diagrams and cross-reference against the diff. Flag any diagram entities that were renamed, split, removed, or moved in the code."
verdicts.reasoning: Both quoted skill sentences verified verbatim at the claimed lines (137 and 168). KICKOFF 1236-1237 names two of the skill's own unconditional numbered steps: Step 2's opening instruction and Step 1.5 item 4. Neither is optional, mode-selected, or scoped by the invocation — 'each doc' is the same universe the skill discovers itself in Step 1 item 3, and diagram drift additionally has a footer rule at line 403 ('**Diagram drift is advisory.** Flag stale diagrams in the PR body but do not auto-edit ASCII art or Mermaid blocks'). I considered refuting this as incidental summary phrasing rather than methodology, since 'sync each doc against the diff' is close to just naming what the skill is for. It survives on the second clause: 'check the architecture diagrams for drift' names a specific internal sub-step by its own terminology, which is the re-listing-internal-phases pattern. Severity medium, not high — it is one clause pair, and duplicating it creates no risk of divergence, only length.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:234-235 "**CRITICAL — NEVER CLOBBER CHANGELOG ENTRIES.** This step polishes voice. It does NOT rewrite, replace, or regenerate content." — restated at SKILL.md:38 "- Overwrite, replace, or regenerate CHANGELOG entries — polish wording only, preserve all content" (under the front-matter **NEVER do:** list) and again at SKILL.md:396 "- **Never clobber CHANGELOG.** Polish wording only. Never delete, replace, or regenerate entries."
verdicts.reasoning: All three skill locations verified on disk at the claimed lines; the wording matches. KICKOFF 1238's 'Polish the voice only, never rewrite or regenerate it' is a word-for-word restatement of the skill's single loudest hard rule, which the skill enforces in three places plus two more supporting clauses (line 240 'Never regenerate an entry from scratch' and line 255 'never regenerate one from scratch'). Nothing in the KICKOFF sentence narrows, conditions, or parameterizes the rule. High severity stands: this is the skill's own gate re-derived in the operator prompt, the exact pattern the audit exists to strip. One scope correction to the claim, which I am not treating as fatal: the quoted range 1237-1238 also swallows the em-dash clause '— whether ship wrote it or I did on the manual path', which claim document-release-4 correctly carves out as load-bearing. The redundancy finding applies to 'Polish the voice only, never rewrite or regenerate it' (and, weakly, to 'polish the CHANGELOG entry'), not to the manual-path clause. Any edit acting on this finding must cut the second sentence and keep the em-dash clause.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:245 "If CHANGELOG was not modified in this branch: skip this step." — verified verbatim at the claimed line, inside Step 5.
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed load-bearing, so KEEP. This clause is upstream pipeline state, not methodology: it tells the reader that step 14 runs identically whether the CHANGELOG entry came from `ship` (automated path) or from the operator's own hand-authored entry at the manual path block, KICKOFF 1209-1231 (verified: that block ends at 1231 and explicitly instructs 'write one unified CHANGELOG entry ... Commit both and push so the PR picks them up'). The skill cannot know which path ran. It is genuinely the join between two guide branches, which is exactly the ordering/branching class the guide owns. I probed the weaker reading — that it is mere reassurance, since the skill's own line 245 check keys off whether CHANGELOG was modified in the branch and both paths do modify it — and that is why this is low severity rather than medium: it changes no agent behavior, it prevents an operator on the manual path from assuming step 14 is a ship-only step and skipping it. That is enough to keep, and only just.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:15-16 "You are running the document-release workflow. It runs **after code ships** (committed, PR exists or about to exist) but **before the PR merges**." — verified verbatim. Countervailing: SKILL.md:10 "Proactively suggest after a PR is merged or code is shipped."
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed load-bearing, so KEEP — but on narrower grounds than the claim gives. I grepped the whole skill for merge/open/branch state: the only hits are line 5 ('but before it merges'), line 16 ('before the PR merges'), line 10 (the description, which says the opposite), line 72-73 (the base-branch abort), and line 373 (`git merge-base`, unrelated). So 'PR still open' is asserted in orientation prose and in the description-summary, contradicted by the description's proactive trigger at line 10, and never gated anywhere in the ten numbered steps. The KICKOFF clause does two things the skill cannot: it places step 14 in the pipeline relative to whatever later step merges the branch (cross-step scheduling the guide owns), and it resolves the skill's own internal tension between line 10 and line 16. Note the honest caveat: the first half, 'Run from the feature branch', overlaps the abort gate at line 72 and is covered by claim document-release-6; what is genuinely load-bearing here is 'with the PR still open'. Low severity.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:72-73 "1. Check the current branch. If on the base branch, **abort**: \"You're on the base branch. Run from a feature branch.\"" — verified verbatim at the claimed line, as Step 1 pre-flight item 1.
verdicts.reasoning: The skill enforces this itself as a hard abort in its very first numbered action, and it needs no operator input to do so — Step 0 (lines 44-66) detects the base branch on its own from the remote/PR metadata. KICKOFF 1239 therefore re-derives an already-enforced gate. I kept it at low rather than medium for the reason the claim gives, which I agree with on reading the surrounding text: the clause is phrased as operator-facing rationale ('because it needs the unmerged diff' — explaining why the run would die), not as an instruction to the agent, and the causal 'why' is not stated in the skill. That rationale is the only non-duplicated atom in the sentence, and it is not load-bearing on its own since the abort fires regardless.
